row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Holding 11:14-21 inside a single long 11:1-21 courtyard-and-oracle row, with the word-event at 11:14 disclosed only as internal texture, was weighed as an alternative reading. It was not taken because 11:14 is a strict word-event onset (not a bare transition) and the oracle's own addressee — the scattered exiles — differs from the courtyard men addressed in 11:1-13, which is enough of a class shift to justify treating it as its own formula-bounded row even while the wider vision frame stays open around it. A second rival sits inside this row and is weighed here as well: a seam at 11:16/11:17. This witness records a samekh after MT 11:15 and another after MT 11:16 (single witness), and because the witness enters each mark on the verse it stands after, both fall immediately before a verse that carries the long messenger formula כה אמר אדני יהוה — oshb:Ezek.11.16 and oshb:Ezek.11.17, two of that formula's 122 verses. Neither seam is licensed as a sub-onset, since a messenger formula opens one only if the people addressed change or the verse just before it finishes on a close-role formula. The addressee holds steady: the son-of-man address and the scattered exiles are named at 11:15 and nothing readdresses the oracle before 11:21. Nor does either preceding verse finish on a close-role formula — MEASURED on the pointed witness, MT 11:15 finishes לָ֥נוּ הִ֛יא נִתְּנָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ לְמוֹרָשָֽׁה (oshb:Ezek.11.15) and MT 11:16 finishes בָּאֲרָצ֖וֹת אֲשֶׁר בָּ֥אוּ שָֽׁם (oshb:Ezek.11.16), while in 11:16 and in 11:17 alike the messenger formula stands at the verse's head after לכן אמר rather than at its end. A mark alone cannot stand in for that verse-final formula, so the two samekhs are disclosed for the paragraph structure they corroborate within the row, and the row rests on its strict word-event onset at 11:14 and its verse-final utterance close at 11:21 (MEASURED: נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה closes MT 11:21; oshb:Ezek.11.15, oshb:Ezek.11.21).

Independently, cutting there would leave 33:10-11 as a two-verse row that is not a complete word-event unit, and 33:11's own close-shaped cluster cannot supply the licence the rival onset lacks -- its utterance formula stands mid-verse, at word 5 of that verse's 25, counting from the first, with independent imperatives running on after it, so 33.11 is not a close the rival could stand on, and a mark alone never carries that weight however strong the pe looks. The rival is therefore paragraph-grade, and the disputation runs on as one 'you say ... but I say' unit across 33:10-20, which is the near face on both of this row's seams.

The unit is held as one scene, with the live rival inside it weighed below: the prophet is set down among the bones (37.1-2), questioned and commanded to prophesy twice -- once to the bones, once to the breath/spirit (37.4-6, 37.9), watches the two-stage reanimation (37.7-8, 37.10), and receives the scene's own interpretation as a word to 'son of man' (oshb:Ezek.37.11 וַיֹּאמֶר֮ אֵלַי֒ בֶּן אָדָ֕ם הָעֲצָמ֣וֹת הָאֵ֔לֶּה כָּל בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הֵ֑מָּה הִנֵּ֣ה אֹמְרִ֗ים יָבְשׁ֧וּ עַצְמוֹתֵ֛ינוּ וְאָבְדָ֥ה תִקְוָתֵ֖נוּ נִגְזַ֥רְנוּ לָֽנוּ). Close: oshb:Ezek.37.14 stacks three refrain-grade closes in one verse -- the second-person plural recognition variant ('and you will know that I am YHWH', part of a 21-verse 2mp family sweep), the emphatic 'I YHWH have spoken' close (one of 14 book-wide), and the short utterance signature without the divine-name pair (one of only 4 such short forms in the book) -- וְנָתַתִּ֨י רוּחִ֤י בָכֶם֙ וִחְיִיתֶ֔ם וְהִנַּחְתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם עַל אַדְמַתְכֶ֑ם וִידַעְתֶּ֞ם כִּי אֲנִ֧י יְהוָ֛ה דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי וְעָשִׂ֖יתִי נְאֻם יְהוָֽה, and a pe mark is recorded immediately after this verse (tier-3 single-witness, informing not deciding). Both sides of the following seam were weighed: oshb:Ezek.37.15 opens with the strict word-event formula וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, one of 39 verses carrying that strict form, so the close at 37.14 and the fresh onset at 37.15 corroborate each other from both directions. Both faces of that close are top grade; the row is held at medium because a licensed rival stands inside the span, at the 37.10/37.11 seam.

row.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 40:1 opens with the dateline בְּאַרְבַּ֤ע עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה אַחַ֕ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֻכְּתָ֖ה הָעִ֑יר (“after the city was struck” (web:Ezek.40.1)) -- the fourteenth and last of the book's fourteen year-bearing datelines -- paired in the same verse with the hand-of-YHWH idiom הָיְתָ֤ה עָלַי֙ יַד יְהוָ֔ה and the transport verb וַיָּבֵ֥א אֹתִ֖י שָֽׁמָּה (oshb:Ezek.40.1). This dateline-hand-transport cluster is the strongest onset class the book offers and is also a HARD seam: no row may cross it. It follows immediately, without intervening material, the utterance formula and pe (oshb:Ezek.39.29, single-witness) that close the preceding unit. The frame continues at 40:2 with the header בְּמַרְא֣וֹת אֱלֹהִ֔ים “In the visions of God” (web:Ezek.40.2; one of only three such headers in the book) plus a further transport pair (הֱבִיאַ֖נִי / וַיְנִיחֵ֗נִי (oshb:Ezek.40.2)), and again at 40:3 (וַיָּבֵ֨יא אוֹתִ֜י שָׁ֗מָּה (oshb:Ezek.40.3)) introducing the measuring man. Close side: 40:4 carries no formula-grade close device; the seam at 40:4/40:5 rests on the man's charge, הַגֵּ֛ד אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר אַתָּ֥ה רֹאֶ֖ה לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.40.4) “Declare all that you see to the house of Israel.” (web:Ezek.40.4), read as ending the entry scene before the measuring reed is put to use in 40:5's וַיָּ֜מָד (oshb:Ezek.40.5), the first of an eighteen-verse run of that verb across 40:5-41:5. Both sides are weighed: the onset is the best-evidenced in the whole span; the close is a content judgment (charge-speech versus measuring-action), not a refrain, and is held accordingly.

row.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:18 opens on a said-to-me verse, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י, and then carries בֶּן אָדָם֙ כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.43.18) 'son of man, thus says the Lord YHWH' -- one of the book's 122 messenger-formula verses, and the clearest speech-onset here after the throne declaration of 43:1-9 -- introducing the altar's dedication ordinances. The utterance formula נְאֻ֛ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה (oshb:Ezek.43.19) appears mid-unit at 43:19, read as paragraph-final rather than row-final since the seven-day consecration instructions continue without interruption. Close side: immediately after that utterance the verse carries two consecutive samekh marks, the sole doubled occurrence among the book's marked verses (sweep: 183 verses) -- making 43:27 the best-attested close available and the strongest evidence for ending it exactly here. Both sides converge unusually cleanly here: a messenger-formula onset opposite an utterance-plus-doubled-mark close.

Parashah marks are disclosed in three directions, MEASURED in this witness, which records a mark ON the verse it FOLLOWS. Onset seam: corroboration IS present -- two consecutive samekh marks follow Ezek.43.27, the verse immediately before this row's first verse, and this row's own rationale argues from them. row.boundary_rationale: Onset: Ezek.44.5 opens with a son-of-man address launching an instructional mode; 44.6 and 44.9 both carry the messenger formula, addressed throughout to the same topic (the house of Israel's abominations in admitting uncircumcised foreigners to the sanctuary) with no addressee-class change between them, so neither reopens the row on its own. The unit turns at 44.10 to the Levites' judgment for their prior idolatry: they may minister but may not approach as priests, with the utterance signature appearing mid-paragraph at 44.12 (paragraph-final, not row-final, since no fresh onset follows immediately) and the paragraph closing at 44.14. Close: the pe parashah mark recorded after Ezek.44.14 corroborates that close; the very next verse, 44.15, turns to a different priestly class (the sons of Zadok) with its own utterance signature near its opening -- an addressee-class shift inside the same law section.

Close: the pe recorded after Ezek.44.31 -- the last parashah mark in ch44 -- closes the row; the chapter division at 44/45 coincides here, though it is cited only as context, never as evidence on its own.

The row holds against it on three stated grounds: Ezek.47.6's question looks BACK at the measuring just reported and its motion returns the prophet to the bank inside one scene rather than opening a new one; 47:1-12 reads as a single region with 47:6 inside it as interior texture; and the only further signal at 47:6 is the WEB's mid-verse paragraph, which is tier-4 and never corroborates a seam. Guided-motion verbs stand inside the measuring circuit, though not at its head: MEASURED over the pointed Hebrew witness, Ezek.47.3 does not BEGIN with a guided-motion verb (it opens בְּצֵאת הָאִ֥ישׁ) but does carry וַיַּעֲבִרֵ֥נִי later in the verse, and Ezek.47.4 carries that same form twice. The measuring sequence therefore remains texture inside the single river vision running 47.1-12, disclosed as a one-sentence category deviation rather than split into a separate row (oshb:Ezek.47.5, oshb:Ezek.47.3, oshb:Ezek.47.6).
